models.name: discussion_board_system_configs
models.description:
System-wide configuration table for board-level settings and feature flags.

Stores key-value pairs representing runtime tunable parameters or business policies. Used as a foundation for global configuration, such as toggling features, maintenance mode, upload limits, or descriptive metadata that governs the entire discussion board. No foreign keys as this is an isolated domain for maintainability. Allows for future extensibility and immediate board-wide change management without database migrations. All updates are auditable thanks to temporal fields.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for each configuration entry.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique key identifying the configuration item, e.g., 'feature_upload_enabled', 'max_file_size_mb'. Must be unique for each system setting.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: Configuration value as a string. May contain JSON or plain scalar values depending on application logic. Stores the current value for the given setting.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable explanation of this setting's business role and usage.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of configuration entry creation for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this configuration record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If set, marks this configuration as deprecated or inactive; preserves audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_users
models.description:
Registered user identities for standard discussion board participants.

Each user entity represents a distinct account able to post, comment, and upload attachments within the platform. Account includes essential authentication data, such as email and password_hash, for secure login. Created/updated/deleted timestamps track account lifecycle. Only accounts of this type can manage their own content; administrative privileges are not granted by this entity. User data is minimal per privacy requirements, and no extra profile fields or roles are included.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's unique email address for registration and login. Serves as natural key for authentication; must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed user password for secure authentication. Raw passwords are never stored; field holds the hashed value only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of account creation. Immutable after initial registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent account modification, including password or email changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp marking user account as soft-deleted. Nullable; null indicates active account.

models.name: discussion_board_user_sessions
models.description:
Login session records for standard discussion board users.

Each session records an authenticated login event, supporting JWT or refresh token handling for auditing and revocation. Linked to parent user via user_id foreign key, not unique (multiple concurrent sessions per user allowed). Session stores connection metadata (IP address, request referrer, href) for traceability and potential abuse investigation. Session expiration is recorded for proper logout/idle handling.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to authenticated discussion board user. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address recorded at session start for audit and traceability.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full request URL (href) at authentication. Helps with session context and abuse investigation.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer for session initialization. Provides context for user navigation during login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of session creation; marks login instant.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when session was terminated, logged out, or token expired. Null if still active.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description:
Registered system administrator accounts for board governance and moderation.

Admins possess full privileges for content and user management, able to edit or remove any article, comment, or attachment, and manage user accounts. Authentication is via unique admin email and password_hash. Admins act independently of user accounts; no normalization or shared credentials exist between users and admins per requirements. Full lifecycle and soft deletion are supported for audit and compliance.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for administrator authentication. Distinct from user emails; must be unique among all admins.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt password hash for administrator login. Raw passwords are never stored; field holds the cryptographic hash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when admin account was last modified, including password changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete marker; null if account is active, set when account is deactivated or removed.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Administrator login session records for audit and privilege enforcement.

Each record tracks an authenticated admin session, supporting privilege control, JWT/refresh token context, and audit trail. Sessions are linked to the admin via foreign key. IP address, accessed href, and referrer are captured to enable investigation and compliance. Session expiration timestamp provides logout or force-expiry tracking. Multiple sessions per admin are permitted (not unique).

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to parent admin account. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the admin login session for auditing and security review.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full authentication request URL (href) at session establishment.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer at session authentication for user flow tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when this session was created (login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Nullable timestamp marking session logout or forced expiry. Null indicates active session.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main table for user-generated discussion articles on economic or political topics.

Each record represents a single article authored by a registered user. Includes a required textual title and content, as well as audit fields for creation/update and soft deletion. Supports edit/audit history via the related {@link discussion_board_article_snapshots}. Attachments such as images or files are managed by the subsidiary {@link discussion_board_article_attachments} table.

Articles are directly managed as standalone business entities and linked to their author via user ID. Deletion is soft for traceability and moderation. No business-calculated fields are included; statistics or aggregates are handled externally.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Author of the article. References the {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the article, required for submission. Limited to 200 characters, whitespace-trimmed, and sanitized.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full text body of the article, required. Limited to 10000 characters, supports only plain text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Article creation datetime (ISO 8601 UTC). Never changes after insertion.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Datetime of last update to the article content or attachments.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null unless the article is deleted either by owner or admin.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
Attachment metadata and reference table for images or files linked to articles.

Each record indicates a file (image/document) attached to a specific article, capturing both a unique UUID and metadata about the original file, storage, size, and type for validation, audit, and secure retrieval.

Attachments are always managed as secondary to the parent article; they cannot exist without an owning article. This structure supports moderator/admin removal of individual files and business constraints on allowed types. Records reference the owning article, store original filename, MIME type, size, and storage URI, and support soft deletion per article deletion or direct moderation.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article. Indicates which {@link discussion_board_articles.id} this attachment belongs to.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original name of the uploaded file (user-visible), including extension.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the upload, validated and whitelisted per business rules.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Attachment size in bytes. Maximum per requirements is 10MB.

plainFields.name: file_uri
plainFields.description: Storage URI for the actual file (external S3 or local path as configured). Not directly accessible by users.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when the attachment record was created (upload timestamp).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp; indicates if attachment was removed by the article owner or admin moderation.

models.name: discussion_board_article_snapshots
models.description:
Table for storing immutable snapshots of articles, supporting edit history, recovery, and audit trails for moderation.

Each snapshot records a historical version of its parent article, including title, content, the editing user, and all audit timestamps. All fields are captured at the moment of edit or update, providing traceability for changes and supports roll-back or admin review of edited/deleted content.

Snapshots are created on every edit to {@link discussion_board_articles}, referencing the current article. Not editable after insertion; only appended for new versions. Accessible by admin for moderation and compliance auditing.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the target article whose version is being saved. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: editor_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the edit (could be the original author or an admin). References {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_title
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the article title as captured at edit.

plainFields.name: snapshot_content
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the article content as captured at edit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when this snapshot was recorded (edit or moderation time).

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Main comment entity for article-based discussions. 

Stores user comments posted beneath articles on the economic/political discussion board. Every comment is individually created by a registered user and explicitly linked to a parent article and author. The model supports text-only discussion—no nested replies, attachments, or media—ensuring flat, readable discussion per requirements. Each comment may be edited or soft deleted by its author or by admins; a full version history is preserved via companion snapshot table. Audit logging, moderation, and compliance flows refer to this entity for comment lifecycle management.

Foreign keys reference existing user and article tables. Indexing supports rapid retrieval by article and chronological ordering. All lifecycle fields (created/updated/deleted) included. Only authenticated users may comment, as enforced in business logic.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author; the registered user who created the comment. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment content text as provided by the author. Limited to 5,000 characters per business rules. Cannot be blank or empty.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment was originally posted. Immutable, set automatically on creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to this comment. Updates whenever author or admin edits content.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete marker for comment lifecycle management. Nullable; populated when comment is hidden/deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshot table capturing every prior version of a comment.

Stores immutable records of all comment edits for compliance, auditing, and rollback support. Each row reflects a single state of a comment at a specific edit moment. Snapshots preserve all key attributes: article, author, and content body alongside full timestamp information. Indexing supports audit trail queries and moderation review workflows. This table is append-only; rows are never updated or deleted except via data retention policies. Foreign keys echo the primary comment table for robust relational traceability.

Use this table for audit, compliance, and recovery of previous comment revisions; exposed via read-only access in typical application flows.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment whose version is captured. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article for context at edit time. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Original author of the comment at the version's point in time. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The entire comment text as it existed at the point of edit or deletion. Limited to 5,000 characters, never blank. Saved exactly as submitted at edit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp the snapshot was taken (i.e., comment edit or delete event occurred). Set automatically.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional marker if the snapshotted version corresponded to a deletion event. Nullable; otherwise null.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_logs
models.description:
Moderation log tracking all administrative actions on articles, comments, and attachments.

Each event records the type of action performed (remove, edit, ban, etc.), the target entity (article, comment, or attachment) by ID, the acting admin, action rationale, outcome, and exact timestamp. Supports transparent audit trails and minimal compliance needs for this discussion board. Entries are never deleted to maintain historical traceability. The log references existing core entities via type+ID, allowing polymorphic tracking of acted-upon items in a normalized, non-redundant way.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin account responsible for moderation action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of thing acted on ("article", "comment", "attachment").

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the item moderated (article, comment, or attachment).

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Moderation action performed (e.g., "remove", "edit", "ban").

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for this moderation action as entered by the admin.

plainFields.name: outcome
plainFields.description: Result or status after moderation (e.g., "deleted", "edited", "banned", "restored").

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp representing when this moderation action was performed (UTC, ISO 8601).

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
Technical metadata and storage abstraction for all uploaded attachments (images, files) in the discussion board platform.

This model acts as the canonical store for attachment objects, capturing all necessary file and storage characteristics without direct reference to business entities such as articles or comments. Attachments are uniquely identified and managed within this table, enabling seamless handling of files uploaded to articles, comments, or potential future features.

Fields capture original and storage filenames, file size, MIME type, checksum for duplicate/prevention/security, and storage provider details for local or cloud locations. The model supports lifecycle and security management via soft delete, complete audit of creation and update times, and enables orphan cleanup procedures. Foreign keys (e.g., uploader, link references) are not present—business-layer tables provide those indirect linkages. The table is designed for both immediate production deployment and robust future extensibility, enforcing strict data normalization and supporting file security best practices.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Universally unique file identifier for attachment record.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as submitted by user; displayed in download links. Preserves the name provided on file upload.

plainFields.name: storage_filename
plainFields.description: Internal reference or generated filename used for storage (server, cloud bucket, etc.), never exposed to the user. Ensures collision-free and unguessable storage location.

plainFields.name: size_bytes
plainFields.description: Exact file size in bytes as stored. Used to validate application and storage constraints (max 10 MB per requirements).

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: IANA MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Required for attachment accept/serve validation and display.

plainFields.name: checksum_sha256
plainFields.description: SHA-256 hash checksum of file content, used for duplicate detection, integrity verification, and security audit logging. Uniqueness enforces single storage per identical file.

plainFields.name: storage_location
plainFields.description: Provider identifier or physical/cloud storage reference (e.g., S3 bucket, server path, etc.). Used exclusively by backend for file I/O routing. Not visible to application frontends.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of attachment deletion (soft delete). Null if active; set when attachment is removed, orphaned, or expunged. Supports compliance and orphan cleanup workflows.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: File metadata creation timestamp. Set on initial upload and immutable thereafter for audit/compliance purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: File metadata last modification timestamp. Updated on any admin or system change to technical information (not business linkage).
